system.summary: Chinese telegraph code numbers disguised by three different keys, one per correspondent's code book: a tens-digit permutation and subtraction from 9000 (共密), per-place digit substitutions plus 0901 (容密), and a reordered code with pages counted backwards over zero-free numbers (辰密).
system.notes: The forms carry the digits in kanji numerals in a grid, read in columns right to left; the stream is cut into four-digit groups. The first two groups are a clear prefix naming the code book. Three different keys: by the writeup skill's one-key rule they could be split into three targets.

prior_solution.where: None known: the texts are not in Hsueh Chun-tu's edition of Huang Xing's 1916 drafts, which has nothing between 8 and 20 June, nor online (Dudout, juin1916 page). 黃興集 and Li Yuanhong's correspondence not yet checked.

conditions.human_role: Contributed: Brice Dudout read the digits on the JACAR scans (blind re-reading), chose leads and criteria; Claude wrote the solvers, tests and log and proposed hypotheses; Codex made the first 共密 trials. The project checked the keys and reran his controls.
models: OpenAI Codex (early 共密 trials; version not supplied)

solution.what: Contributor: forms read in columns right to left, four-digit groups; first sheets of every telegram, then continuation sheets (about 590 容密 groups); all digits re-read blind by Brice Dudout except 18 of V4B's 22 sheets.
Contributor, 共密: for each of the 10,000 constants K the optimal tens permutation by exact assignment, scored by a CTC unigram/bigram model; K = 9000 and φ = 9761405283.
Contributor, 容密: 90 first-sheet groups too few; on about 590 groups, four per-place digit substitutions annealed into readable text.

Contributor, 容密: 借甸 (3949) for 借款 (2949) exactly when the hundreds gave no carry revealed an additive; exact key (tables + 0901 with carries) computed on N02, N08, N11, N12; rule 90 = 00 added from the groups beginning 90.
Contributor, 辰密: 共密 and 容密 keys failed; permuted-page + permuted tens/units model annealed on N13, N16, N26 (201 groups); exact assignment stuck in false optima.
Contributor, 辰密: the page table found follows the countdown of numbers without a zero, then imposed; 劈 for 力 and 滠 for 灰, both from groups ending 9, gave the rule units 9 = 10.

Contributor: 容密 key from four telegrams reads the other ten unrefitted; 辰密 N05 (not in the search, no prefix) reads through; N16 ends 灰 matching its date; V4B, V4D, V4E never used to find the keys read unchanged; names fit June 1916 office-holders.

Project: his verify.py rerun with python -I: 32/32 published raw texts reproduced; scores 共密 3.492, 容密 3.179, 辰密 3.773 against maxima of 200 random keys (-1.450, -1.665, -1.588) and 200 digit shuffles (-1.224, -1.455, -1.177).

Project: his search_gongmi.py recovers K = 9000 and φ exactly from scratch (3.492; shuffled nulls -1.10, -1.07, -1.09); search_rongmi.py gives K = 0900 with hundreds and tens exact, units equivalent up to the carry, thousands off on 7/8/9 (2.608 vs 3.179 for the published key; nulls -1.10, -1.19).

Project: own decoder written from the stated keys (decode.py, Unihan kTaiwanTelegraph table from targets/sunyatsen/tw.csv) applied to his re-read digits: 2472/2472 groups and 32/32 telegrams identical to his raw texts (共密 555/555, 容密 1306/1306, 辰密 239/239).

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): cipher groups ct_gongmi/rongmi/chenmi.txt; decode.py run over groups.tsv and saved per code as texts/<code>_decryption.md; Dudout's keys copied from NOTES to texts/key.md; his annotated texts and translations linked on his Wenmi pages

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): the three decode files read telegram by telegram: chenmi reads; gongmi (N32, N33, N35) and rongmi (N19b, N21, V4D) carry garbled character clusters that break whole clauses. Per-document C confirmed for both; relabelled decoded, not read; class read in part kept; fraction_read 0.9238 -> 0.11.

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, b21). Step 1, is there a text already: no DECODE record (JACAR source). Brice Dudout's Wenmi pages en/gongmi.html and en/rongmi.html fetched 23 Oct 2026: per telegram a raw decoding, a proposed reading ({x} = probable reading, 〔x〕 = kept unresolved) and an English translation, with a digit table group by group. His repository's messages.json (source of our groups.tsv) was fetched too: the page tables are newer for gongmi, 20 groups re-read by him on the scans (N30, N32, N33, N35; 1847 -> 2847 請, 2104 -> 1104 黃, 8229 -> 8339 同 ...: 一/二/三 look-alikes), texts/gongmi_corrections.tsv. JACAR PDF B03050089500 fetched (the /raw/ content path).

b21_wenmi.py: each proposed reading cut into units and aligned with our decoder's output on the page digits; every plain character equals the figure's own value (0 mismatches in gongmi; rongmi 1, the 偽/僞 table variant of one code); each {x} tested for a one-digit variant of its group: gongmi 21 of 24 are one-digit alternates, rongmi 40 of 55 (the rest supplied from context and bracketed). texts/gongmi_align.tsv, rongmi_align.tsv.

One-digit variants listed for every group kept unresolved (〔x〕). Adopted: N24 group 22, 2530 滠 -> 2520 灰 (tens 三 for 二), '灰日唐宅開會' = 'on the 10th a meeting at Tang's house', after '佳日' (9th) in the same sentence; sense-only, flagged for review. Kept as a conjecture [?垣]: V4E group 23, 8063 圉 -> 8053 垣 (V4D: 曉垣 went to Beijing). Not adopted: the endings of N32 (會逵境), N33 (會城), V4E 覃, N24 攴, N25 收 (signature or date codes; no variant gives a known day code), N36 樨 (variant 望 fits '東械望速運' but rests on sense alone).

N35 sheet 1 read on the JACAR scan (B03050089500 p. 2, rendered at 6x): prefix 〇三六四 一三七八 and groups 1-8 as on Dudout's page; group 8 is clearly 八〇〇七 (8007 噸), so 表 (3007) rests on an alternate digit, not on a misreading of the copy. The 二/三 strokes in this hand are often hard to tell apart (prefix 三 of 1378 written as two slanted strokes).

Readings written (texts/gongmi_reading.md, rongmi_reading.md) with Dudout's punctuation, [x] for supplied, [?x] for unresolved, […] for illegible; English from his page with two adjustments (N24 'on the 10th', V4E '[?(Xiao)yuan]') in texts/gongmi_en.md, rongmi_en.md. Explicit-hole score, one character = one word (b21_wenmi_md.py; Chinese not scored by _check_reading.py): gongmi 41/45 (0.91), rongmi 82/90 (0.91). Both set read, grade B; fraction_read 0.11 -> 1.0.

Verification 4: chenmi (4 telegrams) written out as texts/chenmi_reading.md and chenmi_en.md from the decoder output, punctuated, doubtful characters as [?x]; 19/19 sentences clean on the b21 explicit-hole rule, 5 holes in 239 characters. gongmi and rongmi (unscored, Chinese) re-judged as a reader on their b21 readings: both keep read.

outcome.method_basis: All three keys were found by key searches scored with a telegraph-code language model, without cribs or plaintext (Dudout's method pages); only the form dates served as checks.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b21): all three documents of outcome.texts read (chenmi 239, gongmi 555, rongmi 1,306 cipher groups; 2,100 of 2,100). The holes inside them (gongmi 21 [?x], rongmi 47 [?x] and 6 illegible groups, chenmi 7 doubtful) are named in gaps. Earlier figures: 0.9238 (contributor's counts, 19 Oct), 0.11 (reading audit, 22 Oct, chenmi only).

validation.notes: plaintext is Chinese (telegraph code numbers); no letter model in lang/. The contributor's verify.py random-key and digit-shuffle nulls were rerun instead (2026-10-20).

texts.label: 共密, 9 telegrams, June-July 1916
texts.summary: Telegrams between Huang Xing's circle in Tokyo and the Shanghai group, intercepted in Japan: among them Huang Xing's five conditions to Li Yuanhong (restore the 1912 Provisional Constitution and the old Parliament, no amnesty, Duan's cabinet to resign, move Wang Zhanyuan, bring the party leaders to Beijing; N17). Key recovered by Brice Dudout; decrypted here with an independent decoder from his digit readings.

reading_review.note: v4 check 23 Oct 2026: unscored by the sweep (Chinese). Judged as a reader on texts/gongmi_reading.md: the nine telegrams hold as sentences; b21 explicit-hole score 41/45 sentences clean (0.91), 21 [?x] in 555 characters, the holes in signatures/date codes and names. Keeps read. Earlier (b21): Brice Dudout's readings checked group by group against our decoder; 510 of 555 the figure's own value, 21 one-digit alternates, 3 supplied, 21 [?x].

texts.label: 容密, 14 telegrams, June-July 1916
texts.summary: Telegrams on the arms bought in Japan for Zhejiang (Governor Lü Gongwang): about 10,000 rifles, mountain guns and machine guns, ammunition and payment before 30 June, loans and tobacco taxes as security; Japan will not lend to Beijing before North and South are unified; 'no legal solution without armed force'; the meeting at Tang's house; late June, Duan back to three delegates per province.

reading_review.note: v4 check 23 Oct 2026: unscored by the sweep (Chinese). Judged as a reader on texts/rongmi_reading.md: the fourteen telegrams hold as sentences except N36 (11 holes in 58) and V4B (16 in 265), which still read in outline; b21 explicit-hole score 82/90 sentences clean (0.91), 47 [?x] and 6 [...] in 1,307 units. Keeps read. Earlier (b21): Dudout's readings checked group by group; 1,197 the figure's own value, 41 one-digit alternates, 15 supplied.

texts.label: 辰密, 4 telegrams, June 1916
texts.summary: Telegrams to the Hunanese group's address at 277 Avenue Joffre, Shanghai, including a Hunan division under Zhao Hengti for Li Yuanhong (N16).

reading_review.note: v4 check 23 Oct 2026: the entry pointed at the unpunctuated decoder output (texts/chenmi_decryption.md) and Dudout's web translation; no reading or review. Written out as texts/chenmi_reading.md (punctuated, figure values kept; 盻 -> [盼] supplied as in rongmi; 偕, 一不, 畎, 羶 kept as [?x]) and texts/chenmi_en.md. Chinese is not scored by _check_reading.py; explicit holes, one character = one word (b21 rule, supplied characters also counted as holes): 19/19 sentences clean, 5 holes in 239 characters. Judged as a reader: all four telegrams hold as sentences (Shandong offer to Li Liejun; the drafting of the circular telegram; a reliable division under Zhao Hengti for Li Yuanhong; 300 yuan to Baili). Keeps read, grade B.

texts.label: Japanese Foreign Ministry tables (N01): N01, Brice Dudout
texts.summary: Shanghai → Tokyo (青山南町三ノ五三), May 1916; an appeal from the Shanghai friends to Huang Xing. No prefix. The key is given by two decipherment tables on 外務省 paper kept in the same file (JACAR B03050089200, PDF 16, June 1916): it is identical to the key our search had found without them (see the method) .

reading_review.note: 1 telegram (N01, Shanghai friends' appeal to Huang Xing, 15 one-character signatures), coherent; 6 doubtful of 44, mostly emendations ({艱}, {舉}, names); translation follows.

texts.label: “Qianmi” (乾密) key (C104): N09, Brice Dudout
texts.summary: Tokyo (青山南町三ノ五三) → Shanghai, 6–9 June 1916; Huang Xing. Renumbered “明密” book: page = written page − 11, columns and rows permuted. Key model: S. Tomokiyo’s idea (Cryptiana) ; key recovered in October 2026 (see the Qianmi page and the method).

reading_review.note: 1 telegram (N09, Huang Xing: Yuan dead, attitude here unchanged, will cable when talks look promising), coherent; 4 of 23 doubtful as marked emendations.
